topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Traditional cancer treatments and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine conventional cancer treatment modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy alongside their clinical mechanisms, limitations, and toxicities.

topics.label: Exploiting cellular vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction and kinase inhibitor therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the targeting of hyperactivated kinases and oncogene addiction, detailing small-molecule inhibitor mechanisms, bypass pathways, and acquired drug resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the design and therapeutic applications of engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates directed against cancer cell surface targets.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell-directed therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the principles of tumor immune surveillance and modern immunotherapeutic approaches including checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T-cell therapy.

topics.label: Modern challenges, historical trends, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate broader challenges in cancer therapy, including genomic stratification, historical survival trends, prevention, and emerging ethical dilemmas.
